topline.text: New statutory suspension and exclusion guidance came into force on 26 July 2026 — the framework schools return to in September.
topline.action: Re-read it before term; check your recording and pupil-movement processes line up.

topline.text: Annual 2024/25 exclusion figures are due this month — the headline dataset for the year, not yet published.
topline.action: We’ll circulate the day it lands, with your cohort context.

topline.text: Inclusion signals are converging — SEND White Paper tiers, the new EEF inclusive teaching guide, and the December 2026 inclusion-strategy duty all point the same way MAPs already works.
topline.action: Start your inclusion strategy now — don’t wait for the autumn rush.

diary.text: Statutory suspension & exclusion guidance in force (26 Jul 2026).
New academic year: KCSIE 2026 safeguarding guidance, Ofsted operating-guide changes and FSM expansion all take effect.
Statutory duty: publish your school inclusion strategy.
Education for All Bill — first reading and committee stages.
On the horizon: SEND legislative change; EHCP changes no earlier than Sep 2030.

items.body: Updated guidance for maintained schools, academies and PRUs — including pupil movement — took effect 26 July 2026.
Announced in the May 2026 King’s Speech; will carry the white paper’s legislative changes, including SEND reform.
A new £132.5m programme funds in-school and community enrichment; Ofsted will weigh enrichment in personal development.
items.action: An enrichment offer is now an inspection asset — map what you already run against it.

items.body: “Every Child Achieving and Thriving” proposes tiered support — universal, targeted, targeted plus, specialist — with Individual Support Plans, School Inclusion Bases and an Inclusive Mainstream Fund.

items.lede: Seven principles, and a statutory duty.
items.body: All schools must publish an inclusion strategy from December 2026 and report on how inclusive mainstream funding is deployed.
items.action: Your cohort data is the backbone of a credible strategy — see the tool spotlight below.

items.body: Published 6 July 2026: a two-part model — strengthen universal practice, then adapt thoughtfully — directly supporting the inclusion-strategy duty.

The Difference and IPPR set out four principles of whole-school inclusion and call for £850m over five years for preventative, universal support — modelling suggests it pays for itself by 2030 by reducing the need for around 35,000 EHCPs.
Spring 2025: 3,320 permanent exclusions — a spring-term record — and 312,562 suspensions; the FSM permanent-exclusion rate ran 5.9× that of peers.
Full-year suspensions rose 21% to 955,000 in 2023/24, with persistent disruptive behaviour cited in 51% of cases.
New procedures for inspecting inclusion bases and a similar-schools attainment model from 1 September.
Under the renewed framework, inclusion is judged directly rather than spread across areas — a structural argument in the network’s favour.

The new statutory safeguarding guidance (in force 1 September) removes Annex A so all staff read Part 1, requires an annual review of filtering and monitoring, and strengthens provisions on AI, cyber security and misogyny.
items.action: Refresh your child-protection policy and staff training against the 2026 changes before term.

items.body: From September 2026, FSM extends to all Universal Credit households; transitional protections end and eligibility rechecks are required.

items.lede: Sheffield Ofsted results under the new framework.
items.body: The Star rounded up May–June outcomes; Stocksbridge High rated ‘urgent improvement’ on achievement and attendance/behaviour.
Sheffield City Council reported an improved 2025/26 position — useful background to the funding bid.

box.text: Pupils suspended even once are around twice as likely to be NEET (not in education, employment or training) by age 24.
box.attribution: EPI (2024), cited in IPPR & The Difference’s “Who’s Losing Learning?” — the evidence base the upstream model is built to interrupt.
